import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong candidates based on mean difference and t-statistic
    strong_candidates = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if abs(feats.x[:, i].mean() * 2 - 1) > 0.1 and abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==0, i], feats.x[feats.y==1, i])[0]) > 2.5:
            strong_candidates.append(fid)
    
    # Cluster correlated features
    corr_pairs = [(a, b) for a, b in [
        ("FJDC1", "YIFW13"), ("CNZK2", "BHR10"), ("YIFW13", "YBE10"),
        ("JOEN12", "YIFW13"), ("RMJB3", "YIFW13"), ("FJDC1", "IAX6"),
        ("JOEN12", "RMJB3"), ("IAX6", "YIFW13"), ("YIFW13", "QLP12L"),
        ("YIFW13", "YTMC4L"), ("JOEN12", "SZB15L"), ("FJDC1", "YBE10"),
        ("FJDC1", "YTMC4L"), ("YIFW13", "KLAJ17"), ("FJDC1", "KLAJ17"),
        ("UHFH19", "YBE10"), ("THZS1", "YBE10"), ("FJDC1", "RMJB3"),
        ("YIFW13", "SZB15L"), ("RMJB3", "YBE10")
    ] if a in feats.ids and b in feats.ids]
    
    # Create feature matrix for clustering
    feature_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in strong_candidates]
    X_cluster = feats.x[:, feature_indices]
    
    # Cluster features based on correlation
    if len(strong_candidates) > 1:
        # Compute correlation matrix
        corr_mat = np.corrcoef(X_cluster.T)
        # Use Agglomerative Clustering to group highly correlated features
        clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=max(1, len(strong_candidates)//2),
                                             linkage='average')
        clusters = clustering.fit_predict(1 - np.abs(corr_mat))  # Convert to distance
        
        # Select representative from each cluster (highest mean difference)
        drivers = []
        seen = set()
        for i, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):
            if cluster_id not in seen:
                drivers.append(strong_candidates[i])
                seen.add(cluster_id)
    else:
        drivers = strong_candidates[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    unique_drivers = []
    for d in drivers:
        if all(np.abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(d)], feats.x[:, feats.column(other)])[0,1]) < 0.6 
               for other in unique_drivers):
            unique_drivers.append(d)
    
    # Build regression components
    columns = tuple(unique_drivers)
    products = tuple((a, b) for a, b in corr_pairs if a in columns and b in columns)
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {fid: float(np.abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], feats.y)[0,1])) 
                for fid in columns}
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(unique_drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]),
        columns=columns,
        products=products,
        loadings=loadings
    )
